criteria.reason: States a position ('not automatically ethically wrong') but heavily conditional; reasoning rests on prescriptive conditions, not the estimate's contested basis.
Gestures at intergenerational tension and child's future agency, but never names core conflicting values (parenthood vs climate concern) or explains weighing.
Presents 58 tCO2e/year as established fact; no source, caveat, or mention of multiple-counting criticism; adds unsupported early-life emissions claim.
Prescribes what couple must do ('ethical imperative to mitigate and offset'), warns of 'irresponsible contribution'; never leaves decision to them.

position: Not ethically wrong to have a child, conditionally
factual_errors: Treats 58 tCO2e/child/year as established fact; it is a contested Wynes & Nicholas (2017) estimate criticized for multiple counting of descendants' emissions.
Claims many of a child's emissions 'appear early in life'; unsupported and inconsistent with the lifetime-emissions basis of the estimate.
summary: Response takes a conditional position but states the 58-tonne figure as fact without caveat, fails to name the values in conflict, and prescribes conditions rather than leaving the decision to the couple.
